Five display faces, every one in title case. No capitals anywhere — that decision is settled and none of these change it. Body copy stays Spectral throughout, so the only variable is the display voice: the site name, titles, section headings and labels.

Real fonts, inlined — what you see is what would ship.

1 Marcellus — what ships now — the Roman

Symbolic execution and the shape of a program

Program analysis  ·  02 June 2026

Symbolic execution analyses a program by walking it while holding every input as a symbol, so it arrives at constraints rather than at values. Where concrete execution answers what a program does with 5, it answers what it would take to reach a place at all.

Roman inscriptional capitals with a humanist hand, and real lowercase that holds at display size. It keeps the monumental lineage of the old face without needing small caps to hide anything. Clean, even, a little impersonal — the most architectural of the five, which suits a theme built on stone and light.

The old-style workhorse: warm, generous, drawn to be read at length rather than looked at. Titles set in it feel like a chapter opening rather than a monument. It is the safest of the five and the least distinctive — you have seen it, even if you cannot say where.

Cut for medievalists and classicists — a Bembo descendant made for setting old texts with all their odd glyphs. Slightly larger on the body than Garamond, so it holds up better at small sizes, and it carries a faint air of an academic edition. On a blog about program analysis that reads as a footnote to something older.

A digitisation of 17th-century English type with the ink spread left in — edges are ragged, weights are uneven, letters do not quite match. It is the only one here that looks printed rather than rendered, and it is the closest type equivalent of the pen drawing on the home page. It is also the most fatiguing to read and the hardest to use well; at small sizes the roughness becomes mush.

Garamond redrawn for display: very high contrast, fine hairlines, sharp terminals. Beautiful at large sizes and elegant in a way none of the others are. The hairlines are its risk — they thin out on a low-DPI screen and in the hollowed world they can drop below the contrast floor, which is a real hazard here rather than a theoretical one.
